content: The pound-force, often abbreviated as lb, lbf, or lbf, is a unit of force. It is approximately equivalent to the gravitational force exerted on a mass of one avoirdupois pound at the Earth's surface. In such cases, small variations in Earth's gravitational field, which can differ by up to 0.5% depending on location, were considered negligible. However, in the 20th century, the need for a more precise definition of the pound-force arose. To address this, a standardized value for gravitational acceleration was established. Today, the standard acceleration due to gravity is defined as 9.80665 m/s² (approximately 32. Alternative values, such as 32.16 ft/s² (approximately 9.80237 m/s²), have also been used historically. Using the standard gravitational acceleration and the definition of the international avoirdupois pound, the pound-force can be precisely defined. The avoirdupois system defines one pound (as a unit of mass) as being equal to 16 avoirdupois ounces. Similarly, one ounce-force is defined as one-sixteenth of a pound-force. In certain fields, such as structural engineering, the term pound is almost exclusively used to denote a unit of force rather than a unit of mass. In these contexts, the preferred unit of mass is the slug, which is defined as lbf·s²/ft. In other contexts, the term pound may refer to a unit of mass. To avoid confusion, the terms pounds-force (lbf) and pounds-mass (lbm) are used to distinguish between the two. There are three common foot-pound-second (fps) systems of units used for calculations involving mass and force. These systems are summarized as follows: 1. In the engineering fps system, the weight of one pound-mass on Earth's surface is approximately equal to one pound-force. However, this convenience comes at the cost of requiring an additional factor, denoted as gc, when applying Newton's Second Law (F = ma). This factor is typically taken as 32.17405 lb·ft/(lbf·s²). 2. The gravitational fps system is a coherent system of units. By using the slug as the unit of mass, it eliminates the need for the gc factor, ensuring consistency in calculations. 3. The absolute fps system is also a coherent system of units. It aligns with the SI (International System of Units), which is based on the absolute metric system.
